best_parts: node p1_t1 and p3_t1: name the tempting model ('Surgery feels decisive', 'tamoxifen is the drug you learn first') before the refutation, then offer 'Show me the reasoning' (agency) and a sure_note
node p7 (SERM contrast): the reversed-tissue option 'Raloxifene raises it; tamoxifen does not' is a true look-alike trap, so the key is not findable by form
node p1 hint ladder: hint asks what the treatment must do before the knife, without naming the answer
flaws: node p2: only two real choices (one trap, one correct) plus hint; the stem ('which comes next') gives the key away once p1 is answered, and the probe does not test a second wrong model

node p5: correct label is the longest and most specific option ('No routine metastatic scan; start endocrine therapy'), so the key is findable by form (DP1); stem is close to the S3 early-cancer staging probe
nodes p8 (TR25) and p5 (TR5): each trap appears on one probe only in this segment, so recovery cannot be credited within S6; no fast lane or skip option for an expert who already knows the order

best_parts: node ls_p1_ok: 'I know this, skip the worked case' fast lane that still lands on the O9 probe (ls_p2), so the expert path keeps objective coverage
nodes lc_p1 and lc_p2: LCIS is tested in two forms (management, then what LCIS is), and the wrong options (MRM, 'a cancer that needs mastectomy') each map to one TR25 model
nodes tt_p2 and tr_p2: each TR22 and TR6 probe offers a true reversed-action or reversed-drug distractor, so both traps are re-tested in a different form within the segment
flaws: nodes im_p1 and im_p2: stems replay the S3 staging probe ('38-year-old, 1.5 cm ... node-negative, no symptoms') and the S4 t_img probe ('Patient A early, Patient B stage III with bone pain') almost word for word, and test O4, which is not an S6 objective; the learner has just answered these, so this is a repeat for a tired student and off-scope
node ls_p1: the correct option is the longest and carries the purpose clause ('to shrink disease first'), so the key is findable by form (DP1); partial 'Radiotherapy to the breast first' is dominated
node im_p2_part ('Patient A only, since she is young') and node tr_p1 partial ('Seen only when given with a taxane'): obviously weaker than the other options, so they add no diagnostic value (DP2)

best_parts: node seq_why: after the key answer, the learner chooses the reason why drugs come first, and the 'surgery is the curative step' option names the exact wrong model (diagnostic, R9)

node tox2: asks the learner to explain the tissue difference (tamoxifen partly oestrogenic in the womb) rather than only pick the drug, with a partial 'both drugs act alike' option that contrasts with the key
node h1_partial: feedback tells the learner to check how oestrogen is made after menopause, so the partial option routes back to the stem's qualifier
flaws: nodes lcis and tr5: TR25 and TR5 each have only one probe in this segment (the trap map asks for two forms), so there is no in-segment retest; tr5 correct label is the longest option ('Staging CT and bone scan, given stage III and pain')

node seq and tr5 stems: the inflammatory picture ('red, warm, swollen, peau d'orange over a third') and the stage III bone-pain patient repeat the S4 t_pair and t_img probes, so the learner re-answers content already tested

most trap feedback (for example seq_t16, h1_t7, tr6_t6) offers retry only and no 'Show me the reasoning' agency, and there is no fast lane, so the path gives a 1 a.m. learner little control over how much they are told

merge_ideas: b's fast lane and two-form trap structure, with a's 'Show me the reasoning' agency on each trap feedback and a's naming of the tempting model before the refutation
c's seq_why explain-the-mechanism probe placed after the sequence key, to replace b's im_p1/im_p2 replay with an S6-only retest of TR16 and the surgery-is-curative model
b's LCIS and TR22 probe pairs, with a's p2 extended to three real options so the TR16 retest is not a two-option probe
drop b's im_p1/im_p2 (O4, replays S3 and S4) and give TR5 and TR25 a second S6 probe in a new form (for example a stage III case with no bone pain, and a classic LCIS contrast with DCIS)
